title: Fyxer explains why its email assistant uses many narrow models
friendlyTitle: Fyxer breaks email help into many small AI jobs
summary: An OpenAI customer case study describes how Fyxer divides email work among 30 to 50 specialised models for classification, intent, retrieval and drafting. Fyxer says 53% of generated drafts are accepted without edits and that user changes feed a preference-training and A/B-testing loop.
friendlySummary: Fyxer uses separate models to decide whether an email needs a reply, find useful context and write the draft. It learns from edits people make.
whyItMatters: The useful design pattern is to break a broad assistant into observable decisions and learn from real corrections. The results come from the vendor and its customer, so teams should validate similar systems against their own privacy rules, tone and error costs.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Small, clear AI jobs can be easier to test than one large request. People should still check drafts and understand how their email data is used.
